props.title: Enter the Ninja

sections.content: Enter the Ninja kicked off Cannon Films' ninja craze, flooding 1980s cinema with black-clad martial artists. Director Menahem Golan's exploitation classic stars Franco Nero (bizarrely dubbed despite speaking English) as Cole, a white ninja fighting corporate thugs in the Philippines. The film established key ninja movie tropes: smoke bombs, throwing stars, and elaborate training sequences. It launched Sho Kosugi's career as cinema's definitive ninja actor, though here he plays the villain Hasegawa. The film's success triggered an avalanche of ninja films including Revenge of the Ninja (1983) and American Ninja (1985).

sections.content: The ninja boom wasn't limited to Cannon Films. Hollywood jumped on the trend with bigger budget productions like The Octagon (1980) starring Chuck Norris and Ninja Assassin (2009) produced by the Wachowskis. Japanese cinema responded with more serious takes on ninja mythology in films like Shinobi: Heart Under Blade (2005). The 80s ninja explosion also influenced kids' entertainment, from Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1990) to numerous martial arts video games. SUBHEAD: The Sho Kosugi Era

Sho Kosugi became the face of 80s ninja cinema after Enter the Ninja. His authentic martial arts background lent credibility to films like Pray for Death (1985) and Nine Deaths of the Ninja (1985). Kosugi's intense screen presence and real martial arts skills set him apart from western actors in ninja roles. His influence extends to modern ninja films like Ninja Assassin (2009), where he played the villainous clan leader.
